introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2025. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) OR SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Non-programmable electronic calculators and Mathematical Formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.
enonce_intro_markdown:
A random sample of 60 children in a clinic had the following distribution of mass in kg

| Mass (kg) $X$ | 5-9 | 10-14 | 15-19 | 20-24 | 25-29 | 30-34 | 35-39 | 40-44 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency $f$ | 5 | 10 | 13 | 12 | 10 | 5 | 3 | 2 |
incertitudes: Regles de choix : la consigne imprimee est Section A obligatoire, puis DEUX questions de la Section B OU DEUX de la Section C, jamais un melange des trois. Le systeme ne sait exprimer que 2 parmi 3 par section ; l'exclusivite B ou C est recopiee dans introduction_markdown mais n'est pas appliquee par les regles_choix.
Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, sans total par question. Le champ points de l'exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions.

12 : les classes (5-9, 10-14, ...) sont traitees avec des bornes de classe 4.5, 9.5, ... ; le sujet ne fixe pas les echelles du graphe : echelles suggerees dans le corrige. 12(a)(ii) : variance avec la moyenne non arrondie (77.1) ; avec la moyenne arrondie a 21.1 on obtiendrait 76.4. 12(b)(i) : graphe a tracer par le candidat, decrit dans le corrige (points a placer).

questions.enonce_markdown: (a)(i) Find, to one decimal place, the mean of $X$. *[4 marks]*
(a)(ii) Find, to one decimal place, the variance of $X$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Variance $=\dfrac{\sum fx^2}{\sum f}-\bar x^2$ (the table of part (a)(i) gives $\sum fx^2=31\,295$).

$\dfrac{31\,295}{60}=521.58\ldots,\qquad\bar x^2=\left(\dfrac{1265}{60}\right)^2=\left(\dfrac{253}{12}\right)^2=444.51\ldots$

$\text{Variance}=521.58-444.51=77.08\ldots$

**The variance is $\approx77.1$ kg$^2$** (standard deviation $\approx8.8$ kg).

(If the rounded mean $21.1$ is used, $521.58-21.1^2=76.4$; the unrounded mean is more accurate.)

questions.enonce_markdown: (b)(i) Draw a cumulative frequency graph for the distribution. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the **class boundaries** $4.5,\ 9.5,\ 14.5,\dots,44.5$ and accumulate the frequencies:

| Upper class boundary | 4.5 | 9.5 | 14.5 | 19.5 | 24.5 | 29.5 | 34.5 | 39.5 | 44.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cumulative frequency | 0 | 5 | 15 | 28 | 40 | 50 | 55 | 58 | 60 |

**Graph.** Suggested scales: $x$-axis, 2 cm for 5 kg from 0 to 45; $y$-axis, 2 cm for 10 children from 0 to 60. Plot the points $(4.5,0),(9.5,5),(14.5,15),(19.5,28),(24.5,40),(29.5,50),(34.5,55),(39.5,58),(44.5,60)$ and join them with a smooth S-shaped curve (an ogive) starting at $(4.5,0)$ and ending at $(44.5,60)$.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b)(ii) From the cumulative frequency graph, estimate the median. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The median corresponds to the $\dfrac{60}2=30$th value. On the graph, draw a horizontal line from $30$ on the cumulative frequency axis to the curve, then read down to the mass axis.

Reading: the curve passes $28$ at $19.5$ and $40$ at $24.5$, so $30$ lies a fraction $\dfrac{30-28}{12}$ of the way: $19.5+\dfrac2{12}\times5\approx20.3.$

**The median is about $20.3$ kg** (a reading between $20$ and $20.5$ is acceptable).

questions.enonce_markdown: (b)(iii) From the cumulative frequency graph, estimate the semi inter-quartile range. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Lower quartile $Q_1$: the $\dfrac{60}4=15$th value. The graph passes through $(14.5,15)$, so $Q_1\approx14.5$ kg.

Upper quartile $Q_3$: the $\dfrac{3\times60}4=45$th value. The curve passes $40$ at $24.5$ and $50$ at $29.5$, so $Q_3\approx24.5+\dfrac{5}{10}\times5=27.0$ kg.

Semi inter-quartile range $=\dfrac{Q_3-Q_1}{2}=\dfrac{27.0-14.5}{2}=6.25.$

**The semi inter-quartile range is about $6.3$ kg** (exactly $6.25$ with linear interpolation).
